short_title: Angiopep-2 BBB transfer and partially LRP1-associated transport
species_models: Bovine brain capillary EC + newborn rat astrocyte co-culture; mouse healthy brain 5-min in situ perfusion and capillary depletion; immortalized rat RBE4 EC; LRP1-positive MEF1 and LRP1-negative PEA13 fibroblasts; limited normal human brain capillary western blot and biopsy RT-PCR
molecule_format: Angiopep-2 19aa TFFYGGSRGKRNNFKTEEY, iodine-125 and Alexa488-labeled; activated alpha2-macroglobulin (a2M*), RAP, Angiopep-7, aprotinin, transferrin, lactoferrin, avidin, galanin, BSA, exendin-4, PYY
main_endpoint: Blood-side->brain-side model monolayer transport; mouse perfusion capillary depletion brain parenchymal tracer; LRP1 competition/colocalization; human capillary protein
receptor_specificity: Angiopep-2 decreased LRP1-dependent RAP uptake in LRP1-positive vs -negative fibroblasts; Angiopep-2 inhibited a2M* monolayer transport ~50%; a2M* inhibited Angiopep-2 transcytosis ~26%. Support partial LRP1 involvement, NOT full receptor necessity; no in-vivo LRP1 knockout/rescue
luminal_access: Human brain capillary LRP1 western and brain RT-PCR, bovine BBB model Angiopep-2 luminal application; does not quantify native human ischemic luminal epitope density/polarization
internalization_trafficking: Angiopep-2 colocalizes with LRP1-positive vesicle-like structures, primarily near BBCEC cell surface (Fig7); trafficking path, endosomal fate and exit not definitively mapped
directional_bbb_delivery: YES: apical->basolateral passage in bovine/rate co-culture BBB model and parenchymal tracer distribution in perfused mouse brain; NOT demonstrated exclusively LRP1-dependent in vivo; unrelated peptide controls used
intact_cargo_recovery: Study states intact 125I-Angiopep-2 detected on receiver side (data not shown); radiotracer capillary-depletion parenchymal signal does not by itself demonstrate intact peptide chemical identity in perfused parenchyma or intact attached therapeutic cargo
quantitative_results: Apical->basolateral Angiopep-2 passage ~3x aprotinin, >50x transferrin/lactoferrin in assay; a2M* transport RAP/a2M inhibited ~70%; Angiopep-2 inhibits a2M* transport ~50%, a2M* inhibits Angiopep-2 ~26%; capillary-depleted mouse parenchymal Angiopep-2 radiotracer signal; human brain capillary LRP1 protein
safety_mechanism: Potential physiological displacement of essential LRP1 ligands (a2M* clearance, Aβ, lipidoproteins); broad expression; 2008 paper did not test formal peptide toxicology. 2008 paper shows LRP1 in human cancers/brain microvessels, but not normal BBB luminal-selective protein.
strengths: Biological BBB co-culture; orientation-specific apical->basal transwell; perfusion with parenchymal fraction; competitive receptor evidence; LRP1+/- fibroblast comparisons and human brain vessel protein
limitations: Partial receptor attribution only; a2M* and RAP not perfectly specific genetic evidence; capillary depletion radiotracer can include label/metabolite; intact receiver Angiopep-2 claimed data not shown; n small for some panels; not stroke or native human ischemic BBB. Different molecules assayed at unequal concentrations in some comparisons
figures_tables: PDF pp4-10; Fig1 uptake and capillary depletion; Fig2 P-gp; Fig3 passage/human LRP1; Fig4 RAP; Figs5-6 competition; Fig7 colocalization; Fig8 tumors
evidence_grade: PEPTIDE directional blood->brain model/parenchymal tracer precedent + PARTIAL receptor dependence

short_title: Novel 20-aa L57 binds recombinant LRP1 cluster IV; improves perfused mouse brain-associated tracer vs Angiopep-7
species_models: Recombinant human Fc-fused LRP1 clusters II and IV T7 phage panning and peptide ELISA; mouse plasma incubations; healthy male C57BL/6J in situ brain perfusion and separate intravenous study
molecule_format: L57 TWPKHFDKHTFYSILKLGKH-OH, 20 residues, radiolabeled 125I for brain; biotinylated N-Cys derivative for binding; Angiopep-7 TFFYGGSRGRRNNFRTEEY-OH as actual quantitative in vivo comparator (NOT Angiopep-2); Angiopep-2 pilot/reference
main_endpoint: Recombinant domain binding; binding EC50; mouse brain-associated radiotracer 5-min perfusion and 60-min post-IV; plasma peptide persistence
receptor_specificity: L57 binds recombinant LRP1 cluster IV Ser3332-Asp3779 with plate-ELISA EC50 45 nM; no detectable binding to LRP1 cluster II or ActRIIB-Fc under test. NOT direct intact-cell LRP1 gene knockout or brain perfusion competition. EC50 not biophysical KD.
luminal_access: Plasma-delivered peptide reaches brain-associated radiotracer after perfusion; recombinant ectodomain binding does NOT show full-length native human luminal LRP1 accessibility
internalization_trafficking: No cell-scale L57 endosomal route, caveolar dependency, receptor recycling, or intact release studied; brain-tracer distribution not chemically resolved in parenchyma
directional_bbb_delivery: Brain radiotracer present after 5-min luminal arterial perfusion and 60-min systemic IV; direction consistent with blood->brain uptake, but whole hemisphere counts without capillary depletion cannot distinguish vascular binding, EC retention and true parenchymal delivery
intact_cargo_recovery: Parent L57 stable in mouse plasma at least 20 min by HPLC (separate in vitro), but no LC-MS/HPLC identity of intracerebral 125I signal; no conjugated therapeutic cargo or intact abluminal recovery
quantitative_results: Cluster-IV recombinant LRP1 EC50 45 nM. 5-min in-situ uptake 0.220+/-0.052% L57 vs 0.053+/-0.019% Angiopep-7, n=6, p<0.001 (~4.15x); 60-min IV 0.042+/-0.017% vs 0.032+/-0.020%, no significant difference indicated. Plasma parent persists 20 min.
safety_mechanism: Peptide safety not directly assessed; 20-min plasma stability is not in vivo PK safety; cationic peptide and native ligand interference require measurement
strengths: Phage discovery distinct from Angiopep; protein-specific cluster mapping; synthesized exact 20-residue sequence; measurable mouse whole-brain signal in two administration modes; control domain/protein and weaker Angiopep-7 reference
limitations: No LRP1-null brain perfusion, capillary depletion or brain tracer intactness; Angiopep-7 used as comparator not Angiopep-2; recombinant EC50 not KD; whole-brain IV data nonsignificant; supplement Fig S1/S2 and Table S1 not supplied; assay formats (free/biotinylated/radiolabeled) differ
figures_tables: PDF pp1-5; Fig1 phage panning; Fig2 ELISA; Fig3A in-situ and Fig3B systemic i.v.; Table1 5-min and 60-min % input; supplementary FigS1,S2 not included
evidence_grade: DIRECT CLUSTER-IV LRP1 BINDING + MOUSE BRAIN-ASSOCIATED RADIOTRACER; not established intact parenchymal cargo

short_title: L57 rapid endothelial uptake and favorable 4-h MTT versus Angiopep-7 in culture
species_models: Primary early-passage (up to passage 9) rat pup brain microvascular EC and astrocytes, and PEA10 mouse embryonic fibroblast cells with heterozygous LRP1 disruption; NOT human ischemic BBB, not polarized transwell
molecule_format: FITC-Ahx-TWPKHFDKHTFYSILKLGKH-CONH2 (fluorescent C-terminally amidated L57 analog, unlike Sakamoto original -OH); fluorescein-linked Angiopep-7 A7 CONH2 with beta-alanine spacers; fluorescence-labeled arginine-rich control R8
main_endpoint: Fluorescence microscopy and concentration-response 4h peptide cellular association/uptake, live imaging, MTT cellular metabolic viability at 4h, relative comparisons
receptor_specificity: L57 uptake lower in PEA10 (one WT and one disrupted LRP1 allele), but different cell type from BMVEC/astrocytes; compatible with LRP1 contribution, not controlled isogenic knockout/rescue in BMVEC. Fluorescence may reflect labelled peptide and/or metabolites.
luminal_access: Native rat pup BMVEC culture shows cellular association after extracellular peptide treatment; not proof of functional blood-facing luminal LRP1 in intact adult human BBB
internalization_trafficking: Rapid L57-associated fluorescence within 1min in live rat BMVEC; diffuse cytoplasmic and perinuclear distribution after incubations; no specific route (PICALM/PACSIN2/caveolae), no receptor-colocalization, no basolateral release
directional_bbb_delivery: No polarity or BBB transcytosis measured. Entire study compares uptake in nonpolarized monolayer/plates; never tested intact L57 or therapeutic cargo blood->brain flux
intact_cargo_recovery: No chromatography or LC-MS of intracellular intact L57 or abluminal receiver, FITC signal alone cannot demonstrate unchanged peptide
quantitative_results: 4h cellular uptake 10uM Fl-L57 >Fl-A7 in BMVEC (p=0.0082) and astrocytes (p=0.013), PEA10 p=0.075; 30uM L57 BMVEC fluorescence saturated and excluded; Fl-A7 reduced 4h MTT viability at 10-100uM in BMVEC, while Fl-L57 near vehicle; no chronic/systemic safety
safety_mechanism: MTT shows L57 favorable short-term cellular metabolism in tested cell cultures at 3-30uM; NOT proof of low in vivo toxicity or LRP1-pathway safety; Angiopep-7 cytotoxicity is NOT Angiopep-2 cytotoxicity
strengths: Independent rat endothelial uptake and viability confirmation; equal-concentration A7 comparator and positive R8; live-cell timing; multiple cell types with receptor expression gradient
limitations: 4-hour short-term assay; primary immature pup culture, no TEER/polarized BBB; cell lineage confounding of PEA10; differing fluorophore attachment/termini, dose saturation, uptake fluorescent tag != intact chemical peptide. Peer-reviewed article includes supplements not provided.
figures_tables: PDF pp12-18 Figs1-6 and Table1; Fig4 minute time course, Fig5 uptake/dose, Fig6 MTT, Table1 derivatized peptide identities
evidence_grade: INDEPENDENT CELLULAR UPTAKE AND SHORT-TERM TOLERABILITY; NOT a transcytosis or efficacy assay
